question: Roughly how many litres of rain fall on a football pitch in a year of London weather, in millions?
answer: About 4.3 million litres: every millimetre of rain puts a litre on each square metre.
move: Turn rainfall into volume: one millimetre on one square metre is a litre.
ask: How much rain falls on my own roof in a year?
trap: A few thousand litres, picturing puddles instead of depth times area.
hint: A millimetre of rain on a square metre is one litre.
steps: London gets about 600 mm of rain a year.
1 mm of rain on 1 m² is exactly 1 litre.
source: Met Office, UK climate averages, London
reference: Met Office, UK climate averages 1991–2020, London, annual rainfall
